newsitem.title: USA: Orphan Medical expands Busulfanex trials.
newsitem.headline: Orphan Medical expands Busulfanex trials.

text.p: Orphan Medical Inc said Tuesday it will expand the number of patients to be enrolled in its Phase II/III trials for Busulfanex for injection as required by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
As a result, the company estimates the additional clinical data will delay submission of its New Drug Application (NDA) for Busulfanex until the second half of 1998 from the second half of 1997.

"While the FDA is requiring more data, the Phase II trial currently in progress is going very well and data collected to date support our hypothesis that Busulfanex is effective in combination with other cytotoxic agents as a preparatory regimen for bone marrow or peripheral blood stem cell transplantation," said president Bertram Spilker.

"There appears to be increased safety with the intravenous form of busulfan and the additional data should determine if this is true. If so, it could help us obtain improved product labeling," Spilker added in a statement.

Busulfanex is an injectable product being developed by Orphan Medical for use as a preparatory regimen in bone marrow transplants. Bone marrow transplants are currently being used to treat leukemias and lymphomas and are being studied for treatment of solid tumors, such as tumors associated with breast cancer.
An oral form of the drug is currently available, but severe nausea and vomiting accompany the use of oral busulfan, as it is known, making accurate measurement of dosing difficult.
